header: Resolve FIPS endpoint connectivity issues in private hosted zones
content:
FIPS endpoints work with Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collections that have public access. For
newly created VPC collections that use newly created VPC endpoints, FIPS endpoints function
as expected. For other VPC collections, you might need to perform manual setup to ensure FIPS
endpoints operate correctly.
To conﬁgure FIPS private hosted zones in Amazon Route 53
1.
Open the Route 53 console at https://console.aws.amazon.com/route53/.
2.
Review your hosted zones:
a.
Locate the hosted zones for the AWS Regions your collections are in.
b.
Verify the hosted zone naming patterns:
• Non-FIPS format: region.aoss.amazonaws.com.
• FIPS format: region.aoss-fips.amazonaws.com.
c.
Conﬁrm the Type for all of your hosted zones is set to Private hosted zone.
3.
If the FIPS private hosted zone is missing:
a.
Select the corresponding non-FIPS private hosted zone.
b.
Copy the Associated VPCs information. For example: vpc-1234567890abcdef0 | us-
east-2.
c.
Find the wildcard domain record. For example: *.us-east-2.aoss.amazonaws.com.
d.
Copy the Value/Route traﬃc to information. For
example:uoc1c1qsw7poexampleewjeno1pte3rw.3ym756xh7yj.aoss.searchservices.aw
4.
Create the FIPS private hosted zone:

a.
Create a new private hosted zone with the FIPS format. For example: us-east-2.aoss-
fips.amazonaws.com.
b.
For Associated VPCs, enter the VPC information you copied from the non-FIPS private
hosted zone.
5.
Add a new record with the following settings:
a.
Record name: *
b.
Record type: CNAME
c.
Value: Enter the Value/Route traﬃc to information you copied earlier.
Common Issues
If you experience connectivity issues with your FIPS-compliant VPC endpoints, use the following
information to help resolve the problem.
• DNS resolution failures - You cannot resolve the FIPS endpoint domain name within your VPC
• Connection timeouts - Your requests to the FIPS endpoint time out
• Access denied errors - Authentication or authorization fails when using FIPS endpoints
• Missing private hosted zone records for VPC-only collections
To troubleshoot FIPS endpoint connectivity
1.
Verify your Private Hosted Zone conﬁguration:
a.
Conﬁrm that a Private Hosted Zone exists for the FIPS endpoint domain
(*.region.aoss-fips.amazonaws.com.
b.
Verify that the private hosted zone is associated with the correct VPC.
For more information, see Private hosted zones in the Amazon Route 53 Developer Guide,
and Manage DNS names in the AWS PrivateLink Guide.
2.
Test DNS resolution:
a.
Connect to an EC2 instance in your VPC.
b.
Run the following command:

nslookup collection-id.region.aoss-fips.amazonaws.com
c.
Conﬁrm that the response includes the private IP address of your VPC endpoint.
For more information, see Endpoint policies, and DNS attributes in the Amazon VPC User
Guide.
3.
Check your security group settings:
a.
Verify that the security group attached to the VPC endpoint permits HTTPS traﬃc (port
443) from your resources.
b.
Conﬁrm that security groups for your resources permit outbound traﬃc to the VPC
endpoint.
For more information, see Endpoint policies in the AWS PrivateLink Guide, and Security groups
in the Amazon VPC User Guide .
4.
Review your network ACL conﬁguration:
•
Verify that network ACLs permit traﬃc between your resources and the VPC endpoint.
For more information, see Network ACLs in the Amazon VPC User Guide.
5.
Review your endpoint policy:
•
Check that the VPC endpoint policy permits the required actions on your OpenSearch
Serverless resources.
For more information, see VPC endpoint permissions required, and Endpoints policies in
the AWS PrivateLink Guide.
Tip
If you use custom DNS resolvers in your VPC, conﬁgure them to forward requests for
*.amazonaws.com domains to the AWS servers.
